newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani journalist said facing court martial.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani journalist said facing court martial.

text.p: A Pakistani journalist detained by security authorities a month ago is facing a secret court martial on unspecified charges, his lawyers said on Monday.
They said they had learnt about the trial of Humayun Far on Monday during a secret hearing by a civilian provincial high court.
The court discharged a habeas corpus petition for the journalist after being told that the court martial had already begun under a military law, the lawyers said.
They declined to give details of Monday's proceedings before Lahore High Court Judge Mumtaz Ali Mirza, saying they were following a court order for secrecy.

Attorney General Chaudhary Farooq Ahmed had earlier asked for the hearing to be in camera because "serious charges were levelled against Hamayun Far which were linked with security of the country", according to official APP news agency.
Far, Islamabad bureau chief of the Urdu-language newspaper Mashriq, was picked up by plainclothesmen near his home on June 28 and has been held incommunicado.
The journalists' unions have called the arrest an attack on press freedom and demanded that Far be tried in an open court if there are any charges against him.
